title: Nano CTM parity: the synchronization readout wins, but a single-tick pair-product control takes most of the win
hypothesis: On cumulative (prefix) parity, at matched core / internal ticks / parameters / steps, the Continuous Thought Machine's neuron-pair SYNCHRONIZATION readout is not doing the work the paper attributes to it: a last-tick or mean-over-ticks readout on the SAME recurrent core, and a plain GRU with a last-state readout, will land within seed-to-seed noise of it, i.e. the win is recurrence depth (T), not neuron-timing synchronization.
question: Is neuron-timing synchronization the signal in a CTM, or is the sync readout just a proxy for recurrence depth (or for something even cheaper)?
method: Hand-rolled nano CTM in pure PyTorch (no code from SakanaAI/continuous-thought-machines). Shared core for four of five arms: a 12-bit binary string is presented STATICALLY as token+position embeddings; at each of T internal ticks the model forms a query from its own post-activations, attends over the 12 bit-slots, feeds [z_{t-1}, o_t] through a synapse MLP to pre-activations a_t, keeps a rolling window of the last M=4 pre-activations per neuron, and passes each neuron's private history through its OWN small MLP (4->8->1, one per neuron, N=64 neurons). ONLY the readout differs, each a single linear projection to 12x2 prefix-parity logits: (a) sync = CTM synchronization matrix, decay-weighted time-average of 256 neuron-pair products over the tick history (numer_t = r*numer_{t-1} + z_i z_j, denom_t = r*denom_{t-1} + 1, S = numer/sqrt(denom), learnable per-pair r); (b) last = last-tick post-activation vector (64-d); (c) mean = mean post-activation over ticks (64-d); (e) pairlast = ADDED CONTROL, the same 256 neuron-pair products evaluated at the LAST TICK ONLY (same quadratic feature, same dimensionality, zero time-integration); (d) gru = plain GRUCell core with last-state readout, no per-neuron history MLPs. Iso-parameter: the sync arm is the reference (55,800 params) and every other arm's free width is integer-searched to match it (last/mean synapse hidden 286 vs sync's 256; GRU hidden 109); realised spread across all 30 runs 0.46%. Loss is the CTM's own two-tick objective (mean of the loss at the min-loss tick and at the max-certainty tick), applied identically to every arm; evaluation reports the paper's max-certainty-tick prediction on a fixed 2000-string held-out set shared by all runs (final-tick numbers also recorded, same ranking). Held fixed: 475 steps, batch 64, AdamW lr 3e-3 (warmup+cosine), wd 0.01, grad-clip 1.0, identical seeded batch stream per seed, identical fixed 256-pair subset. 5 arms x T in {4,16} x 3 seeds = 30 runs. run.py times every (arm,T) cell first and then picks ONE global step count for all 30 runs so no arm is ever silently given more optimisation than another.
architecture: hand-rolled nano Continuous Thought Machine: attention over bit-slots + synapse MLP + 64 per-neuron history MLPs (M=4), 5 swappable readouts, 0.056M params, iso-parameter to 0.46%

dataset.name: synthetic random binary strings, cumulative (prefix) parity
dataset.source: generated in run.py by torch.randint with fixed generator seeds; 2000-string held-out eval set at generator seed 999

task: cumulative/prefix parity of a 12-bit binary string presented statically (12 binary outputs per string); metric = prefix-parity bit accuracy at the max-certainty internal tick, chance 0.5
compute: CPU 1 thread, 652s (10.9 min) for 30 training runs + calibration + evaluations

metrics.headline: at T=16 (bit acc, chance 0.5, 3 seeds): sync 0.674 > pairlast 0.652 > last 0.618 > mean 0.577 > gru 0.568; sync-minus-last +0.056 is seed-separated, but the single-tick pair-product control takes 0.034 of that 0.056 (and ties sync outright at T=4, 0.685 vs 0.687), so the quadratic feature map - not time-integration - is what pays; every arm gets WORSE from T=4 to T=16

result_summary: The pre-registered null was refuted and then the win was re-attributed. (1) SYNC IS NOT DECORATION: at matched core, params (0.46% spread), ticks, steps and batch stream, the CTM synchronization readout beats a last-tick readout on the identical core by +0.056 bit accuracy at T=16 and +0.058 at T=4, fully seed-separated at T=16 (worst sync 0.667 > best last 0.638), and beats an iso-parameter GRU with last-state readout by +0.105, seed-separated at both tick counts. (2) BUT IT IS NOT SYNCHRONIZATION. The added control - the same 256 neuron-pair products evaluated at the LAST TICK ONLY, zero time-integration, same dimensionality, same params - ties sync at T=4 (0.6848 vs 0.6866, a 0.002 gap against a 0.02 seed sd) and trails by only 0.022 at T=16 with fully overlapping seeds (pairlast best 0.675 > sync worst 0.667). Decomposing the sync-over-last gap: the quadratic pair expansion is worth +0.056 (T=4) / +0.034 (T=16), the time-integration on top of it is worth +0.002 (T=4) / +0.022 (T=16, not seed-separated). So roughly 60-100% of the CTM readout's advantage is a fixed random QUADRATIC FEATURE MAP over neuron pairs, not the neuron-timing synchronization the paper names as its central representation. (3) RECURRENCE DEPTH BUYS NOTHING AT THIS BUDGET: every single arm is flat-to-worse from T=4 to T=16 (sync -0.013, last -0.011, gru -0.021, pairlast -0.033, mean -0.063), so the backlog's dichotomy ('sync, or just recurrence depth?') has a third answer here - neither; it is the readout's feature map. (4) TIME-AVERAGING THE HIDDEN STATE IS ACTIVELY HARMFUL: the mean-over-ticks readout loses the most from extra depth and at T=16 drops BELOW the plain last-tick readout, nearly to GRU level - but multiplying neuron pairs and THEN averaging (sync) does not suffer this. (5) The per-neuron history MLPs are load-bearing: last vs gru, same readout and same attention and same params, is +0.049 at T=16. (6) The accuracy differences are entirely 'how deep a prefix does it crack': every arm is at exact chance beyond a cliff and near-perfect below it; effective solved prefix depth at T=16 is sync 4.19, pairlast 3.69, last 2.85, mean 1.87, gru 1.69 out of 12, and final training loss ranks identically (0.444/0.478/0.513/0.569/0.585), so this is optimisation progress, not an eval artifact. CAVEATS, and they are large: heavily shrunk to fit a 12-minute CPU box - 12 bits (backlog asked 24-40), 475 steps, 0.056M params, T<=16 against the paper's 75-100 ticks; NO arm comes close to solving the task (exact match <= 0.007), so every conclusion is about early-training progress at matched compute, not converged performance; one hyperparameter setting (lr 3e-3, batch 64) picked by a short pilot on the sync arm and not tuned per arm; 3 seeds; one fixed 256-pair subset shared by both quadratic arms (pair-subset variance unmeasured). A discarded 2-seed pilot that also covered T=8 reproduces the ordering and the declining depth trend (T=8: sync 0.697, pairlast 0.679, last 0.667, mean 0.618, gru 0.594).

novelty_check.conclusion: The architecture is fully published; this specific ablation is not. The CTM paper (2505.05522, NeurIPS 2025) defines the synchronization matrix S^t = Z^t (Z^t)^T (Eq. 5) and its learnable exponential decay (Eq. 9-10) and runs the 64-length cumulative-parity demo, but its baselines are whole-architecture LSTMs - it never swaps the READOUT on a fixed core. A direct read of the paper HTML found only a footnote, 'We did begin with snapshot representations but struggled to get stable behavior owing to the emergent oscillatory behavior of neurons', an anecdote with no quantitative comparison and no table. To our search, nobody has published (a) sync vs last-tick vs mean-over-ticks vs plain-GRU readouts on an IDENTICAL core under iso-parameter / iso-tick / iso-step control, or (b) the single-tick pair-product control that separates 'quadratic feature map' from 'synchronization over time' - which is the control that actually moves the conclusion here. arXiv/OpenAlex APIs 403 from this environment (scripts/novelty_check.py returned 'unchecked'); verdict rests on web search plus a direct read of the paper HTML.
